notes.text: **Merged by the operator seat** — review: Reviewed against all five Done-when items; every one met, and this is the seam two tracks depend on so I read it harder than its size suggests. effectiveTools(profile, task, board) is pure, in src/model.js, returning {tools, dropped} where dropped is {tool, source, reason} — returned rather than swallowed, so a caller can say what it took away. The narrowing rule is right: kb.tools and kb.mcp intersect with the profile's grant, anything the card asks for that the profile lacks is dropped and recorded, and both keys absent — which is every card today — returns the grant untouched. Two things I would have asked for and did not have to. The unused  parameter carries an eslint-disable naming exactly why it is there: an extension point #223 and #217 read and this card does not, declared honestly instead of stubbed — and a stub is precisely what would have invited the second derivation this card exists to prevent. And  is handled as 'this harness has no per-command allow-list' (Codex, where the sandbox is the policy) rather than crashing or treating it as empty. The test that matters most is named for the promise: 'every shipped profile launch line is byte-identical to the pre-seam one'. Also covered: the returned list is a copy so a caller cannot mutate the profile grant, and kb.tools and kb.mcp composing on both axes at once. Verified myself: CI green (test + packed artifact), lint clean, 1066 tests on the branch. Scope honoured — no posture, no capability map, no new configuration key, and src/dispatch.js now asks this function instead of reading allowed_tools itself., checks: green, method: squash

residual_risk: kb.tools/kb.mcp are read but not validated anywhere (not in DEFAULT_KB, no hkb doctor check) - deliberate, since the card forbids shipping a new configuration key; whichever sibling makes them real should add the validation.

The kb.mcp rule (a list of server names, each becoming mcp__<server>__* and filtering MCP grants) is a first cut - #223 owns MCP posture and may want a different shape; it should change effectiveTools rather than add a second path.

src/hook.js, src/track.js, src/doctor.js and src/init.js still read profile.allowed_tools, but none of them builds a launch (guard policy, an Agent-capability check, doctor advice, template rendering).
docs/wiki pages covering model.js/dispatch.js are flagged stale by the wiki check; the whole set was already stale before this branch and docs/ is outside this card's kb.paths.

results.summary: effectiveTools(profile, task, board) in src/model.js is now the single pure derivation of a launch's tool list, returning { tools, dropped } where dropped is [{ tool, source, reason }]. A card narrows, never widens: kb.tools and kb.mcp intersect with the profile's allowed_tools, and anything the profile does not grant is dropped and recorded rather than granted (wildcards in a grant, e.g. `Bash(git *)` or `mcp__x__*`, cover the narrower thing a card asks for). src/dispatch.js expandLaunch no longer reads profile.allowed_tools: it takes an optional 4th arg { task, board } and spends effectiveTools for both {allowed_tools} shapes (the list form and Copilot's repeated --allow-tool= form); called without it, every existing caller's expansion is unchanged. spawnWorker passes the card and ctx.cfg, returns tools_dropped on every result path, and the tick logs it at spawn time so a narrowed grant is named instead of reaching the worker as a silent dontAsk refusal. No posture, no capability map, no stub for either, and no new configuration key: DEFAULT_KB is untouched, so kb.tools/kb.mcp are honoured if present but ship as nothing. For #223 and #217: plug into effectiveTools — the signature already takes the profile, the card and the board config, so neither of you has to change it, and neither should touch expandLaunch. PR: https://github.com/emyann/harness-kanban-board/pull/263
